key_insight: High-pressure high-temperature synthesis greatly extends La solubility in Sr3Ir2O7, enabling new magnetic and electronic states beyond what ambient-pressure methods can access.
engineering_relevance: This shows that synthesis route can be as important as composition for tuning correlated oxide properties, which is valuable for designing electronically and magnetically functional materials.
method: Prepared nominal (Sr1-xLax)3Ir2O7 crystals with x = 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, and 0.20 under high-pressure high-temperature conditions.
Used single-crystal X-ray diffraction and SEM-EDX to determine actual La incorporation and phase stability.
Compared magnetic, transport, and structural responses across doping levels.
evidence_signal: Diffraction and SEM-EDX show actual La contents above nominal targets, with ~11% La at nominal x = 0.05 and ~23% La at nominal x = 0.15; the x = 0.20 sample loses the bilayer phase and becomes cubic Sr1-xLaxIrO3.
watch_item: The highest nominal doping destabilizes the target bilayer phase, so extreme La loading may trade off phase purity for higher carrier concentration.
paper_title: Extending the La Solubility Limit in Sr$_3$Ir$_2$O$_7$ through High-Pressure High-Temperature Synthesis
